claim: For uncoloured finite permutation graphs in the adjacency-only signature, let p_n count isomorphism types and q_n the equivalence classes under two-variable first-order logic with counting \(C^2\). For orders \(n=1,\ldots,8\), the pairs \((p_n,q_n)\) are \((1,1),(2,2),(4,4),(11,11),(33,33),(142,140),(776,770),(5699,5654)\). There are no non-singleton classes through order five; exactly two doubletons at order six, both of connected graphs (with 7 and 8 edges respectively); six doubletons at order seven; and at order eight exactly 38 doubletons, two tripletons and one quadrupleton, with every other class a singleton.
integrity: All n! inversion presentations generated directly; exact global vertex-refinement codes and exact NetworkX graph isomorphism. Separate alternate verifier uses hashed signatures solely as corroboration.
scientific_limitations: Finite, exhaustive through eight vertices only. Classical graph-isomorphism counts are prior work. An unlocated earlier counting-logic quotient enumeration remains a priority risk.
title: The eight-vertex counting-logic quotient of permutation graphs
